name: Work (poll jobs in a foreground service, boot restart)
description: The Android host for work@1 poll jobs: an app registers a job (a kernel JobSpec: interval bounds as data, one rule per outcome with fixed / exponential / interval delays, one-time notices per spell, run conditions read from the app's own prefs, foreground + boot restart) whose body is a suspend function that only calls libraries; the loop is the framework's. PollService (foreground, specialUse) drives every job through the kernel's WorkEngine state machine and only carries out its effects (run, sleep, stop, notice, status); START / CHECK_NOW / STOP / INTERVAL commands; a refused foreground start stops quietly; START_STICKY; WorkBootReceiver restarts jobs after a reboot or update when their conditions hold; running-state + state flows per job; the ongoing notification through lib-notifications, rebuilt from the job's state after every run. Fills the platform's android.work placeholder. The engine is cross-port: framework/core/engines/work.ts = ai.amberx.axf.kernel.work.WorkEngine, fixture spec/fixtures/work.json.

android.note: written without a compiler; CI compiles and runs :lib-work:testDebugUnitTest (the kernel engine + WorkConformanceTest and JobRunner were compiled and replayed with a local kotlinc)

web.note: engine + reducer only (no timer host yet); self-test spec/check-work.mts

placeholders.note: The kernel's WorkScheduler contract (axf.work) on WorkManager: constrained periodic work, 15 min minimum, survives process death.
Wall-clock alarms (AlarmManager), exact only when allowed.
Jobs that run after each other.
